chunks: Hadith 4993 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abān, from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That he was asked about a muḥṣan man who committed adultery with a woman, and three men and two women testified against him. He said:

Stoning becomes obligatory upon him. But if two men and four women testify against him, their testimony is not accepted, and he is not stoned; rather, he is given the prescribed punishment, the punishment of the fornicator.

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: Stoning as the prescribed hadd punishment in this specific legal case.
key_terms.الزَّانِي: The fornicator, i.e. the one guilty of zina.
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: The prescribed legal punishment set by the Sacred Law.
key_terms.شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِ: Testified against him in a legal evidentiary sense.
key_terms.مُحْصَنٍ: A legally protected married person whose status affects the hadd punishment for zina.

ai.seo_question: What number of male and female witnesses establishes rajm for zina in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the evidentiary threshold for establishing zina in the case of a muḥṣan offender. It distinguishes between testimony sufficient to establish rajm and testimony that does not establish rajm but still results in the hadd punishment for zina.
